Highest-severity findings are Medium precision/clarity/prose-discipline concerns on agent-executed prompt prose (issue-843/876: no automated regression coverage by design). None is a non-demotable REJECT. Mechanical byte-ceiling check passes (61746 < 61750, no exemption). Shipped skill body is repo-agnostic.
roster_note: type-design-analyzer and pr-test-analyzer gated out (no new types, no tests in this prose-only diff). requesting-code-review is a skill dispatched via a general-purpose Task, not a direct agent type; dispatched that way after the direct-agent form was unavailable. All four always-on reviewers returned an assessment.
diff_profile: prose-only: shipped skill body (skills/implement/SKILL.md, +1 bullet), internal doc (docs/internal/implement-skill.md, +1 paragraph), new changeset (bump: patch, type: Changed). No executable code, no new types, no tests.
checklist_skipped_reason: Prose-only diff with no executable/verifiable code claims; agent-executed prompt prose carries no automated regression coverage by design (issue-843/876). The verification contract is the acceptance criteria plus the single mechanical byte-ceiling check.

phase3_findings.description: The bullet asserts flatly that the vendored checkout is version-pinned (=> rc-127 absent / stale rc-0), but per .github/actions/vendor-plugin/action.yml the version pin applies only to the `fetch` (thin-install) source; `committed`/`self` sources copy from the possibly-PR-head checkout. PRFlow's own runs use source: self, where a branch-committed helper is not necessarily absent/stale. The claim is true for the dominant fetch case but stated as universal.
phase3_findings.defect_signature: overgeneralized-mechanism-claim: vendoring version-pin asserted universally but holds only for `fetch` source
phase3_findings.assessment: Core reasoning technically sound and the three surfaces are mutually consistent with an accurate section cross-reference; the one substantive technical inaccuracy is the universal vendoring claim (should be scoped to fetch/thin-install or note the self/committed exception). Two Medium items (this + skill-body derivation duplication) plus one Low adjacency note. Note: the rule's operative conclusion (helper unreachable) still holds under self/committed via the second, grant-timing mechanism, so this is a precision defect, not a wrong-action rule.

phase3_findings.description: The rule offers 'the existing deferral/Blocked path' as a disjunction with no criterion for choosing between them. Deferral (records follow-up, run may still report Complete) and Blocked (stops) have different completion semantics; if the unreachable helper backs an AC-critical step, routing to deferral rather than Blocked could let the run report Complete with an AC unmet. Mitigated by the existing (referenced, not redefined) deferral/Blocked machinery presumably enforcing AC-completeness, so a clarity gap rather than a new silent path.
phase3_findings.defect_signature: disjunctive-terminal-without-selection-criterion: deferral-vs-Blocked routing left to agent discretion; AC-critical case not distinguished
phase3_findings.assessment: A well-constructed fail-loud rule, not a silent-failure defect. Up-front detection from branch delta (a computable operand already used in phase-2 sweeps via git diff --merge-base) correctly decouples detection from the rc-0 trap; the terminal is loud and named; 'attempt no workaround' bars masking shapes after the work is recorded, not instead of recording it; ordering places detection before any rc-based short-circuit. No Critical/High. One Medium (disjunctive terminal) + one Low (named-signal-without-operationalized-command).

phase3_findings.description: The SKILL.md bullet inlines the full two-mechanism derivation ('Two mechanisms: the vendored checkout is version-pinned...; and config grants resolve at trigger time...') that the docs/internal paragraph also carries and explicitly claims to own ('this paragraph remains the broader statement'). Tension with the instruction-plus-consequence prose rule for skills/** bodies (derivation/worked-example should move to internal docs) and a mirror-fact restatement of B's mechanism facts.
phase3_findings.defect_signature: skill-body-derivation-duplication: SKILL.md bullet inlines the two-mechanism derivation the docs/internal paragraph also carries
phase3_findings.assessment: See comment-analyzer overall assessment above; this is the second of its two Medium findings. Counterpoint (shadow orchestrator): both mechanisms are load-bearing to the rule — they justify 'no need to distinguish' and 'up front' — so a case exists that they belong in the operative body; treated as a non-blocking prose-discipline concern.

phase3_findings.description: The detection instruction names 'branch delta' but, unlike the phase-2 sweep bullets, does not name the concrete command (git diff --merge-base / --name-only) to obtain it. An agent mapping invocations against memory rather than a computed diff could miss an indirectly-modified helper and quietly degrade toward the rc-based path the rule supersedes.
phase3_findings.defect_signature: named-signal-without-operationalized-command: relies on 'branch delta' concept without pointing at the established git diff computation used elsewhere
phase3_findings.assessment: Low because the concept is defined and used a few files away; a cross-reference would close the gap cheaply.

phase3_findings.description: The docs/internal/implement-skill.md paragraph substantially restates the skill-body rule's specifics (branch delta, post-merge grant/vendor timing, stale rc-0, absent/stale/denied identical) rather than being a terse pointer. Satisfies AC6 but creates a coupled mirror that will drift if the skill bullet is reworded; no test pins the two identical.
phase3_findings.assessment: Approve-quality. Change is correct, well-scoped, correctly placed in the shipped skill body per the placement rule, repo-agnostic, and satisfies every AC. Two Low findings (this + 4-byte ceiling headroom) and one Suggestion (prose density), all advisory.

phase3_findings.description: skills/implement/SKILL.md is now 61746 bytes against the 61750 ceiling — a 4-byte margin. AC7 is met (under ceiling, no new exemption), but essentially any future prose addition to this file will trip the RED gate; remedy per CLAUDE.md is trim-not-exempt. Informational for this change.

The added docs paragraph sits immediately after the Grant-timing bootstrap paragraph, which already states grants resolve at trigger time from the default branch; the new paragraph re-invokes the same fact. B mitigates by pointing rather than fully restating, so a mild adjacency-redundancy note, acceptable as written.
phase3_findings.defect_signature: adjacent-fact-restatement: grant-timing mechanism referenced immediately below the paragraph that defines it
phase3_findings.assessment: Flagged for awareness only; not a hard mirror-fact violation.

phase3_findings.description: The SKILL.md bullet is dense with layered consequence clauses; the tail 'This tightens first-refusal only for one this branch introduced or modified' partially re-states the opening scope. Given the 4-byte ceiling margin, tightening would buy headroom. Optional.

The docs/internal/implement-skill.md paragraph restates the rule's mechanics fairly fully rather than pointing tersely; stays on the right side of single-source (names the skill body as runtime home, scopes itself as the broader allowed_tools statement) but is close to a second copy needing same-commit reconciliation if the skill wording changes.
phase3_findings.assessment: Merge-ready APPROVE. All seven ACs met; load-bearing technical claims verified correct against lib/capability-profiles.json (implement profile grants ONLY vendored-literal paths, so the bare repo-relative fallback is denied and the 'unreachable' + path-prefix-ban claims are accurate even in self-repo runs). Placement and consumer-shipping conventions honored; byte ceiling holds. Single minor observation is a maintainability note, not a defect.
